A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MODEM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across additions, relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration results, component ablations, feature visualizations and inference-time measurements in Sections 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds perceptual evaluations, real-world benchmark results, scanning and loss ablations, and efficiency comparisons.

M1.justification: MODEM retains the same DDEM, MOS2D, DAFM, DSAM, two-stage training and losses. Section 4 expands the explanation of ground-truth access and frozen-teacher supervision without establishing a procedural change. Alternative scans and losses are evaluated as ablations.

E1.justification: Section 5.2 and Table 6 add evaluation on NTURain, RESIDE and WeatherStream, substantially extending real-world rain, haze and adverse-weather coverage. Snow100K-Real and RainDrop were already evaluated in v1; the original training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes NAFNet from the desnowing comparison and adds ConvIR and FSNet; Table 3 adds AST. Appendix A.7 newly evaluates MambaIR, FreqMamba and VMambaIR under the all-weather setting. These substantially strengthen comparator coverage. Figure 6's Histoformer variant is relabeled, with its displayed results retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds LPIPS, Q-Align and MUSIQ evaluation, quantitative no-reference assessment of real-world images, and runtime measurements at 512×512 and 1024×1024 beyond the existing 256×256 test. New controlled experiments compare scan choices and loss configurations. The original MODEM training settings and dataset splits are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices A.3–A.6 add resolution-scaling analysis, Morton-versus-Hilbert timing, comparisons among six scanning schemes, correlation/KL-loss ablations and a KL-placement variant. Figure 9 extends the existing feature visualization with additional cases. These directly investigate design choices left substantially less tested in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars or significance tests. v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical significance reporting but introduces no uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 results remain unchanged, including MODEM's average 34.18 PSNR and 0.9452 SSIM, but substantial perceptual, baseline, ablation and timing results are added. ConvIR exceeds MODEM on snow SSIM in Table 2, and WeatherDiff leads RESIDE Q-Align in Table 6. New Snow100K-Real Q-Align entries conflict: MODEM scores 3.5586 in Table 5 and 3.7324 in Table 6.

T1.justification: The SSM decomposition, Morton encoding, modulation equations and loss definitions in Equations 1–14 are retained. v2 adds no mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof; its new scaling discussion interprets runtime measurements.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about degradation estimation, Morton-order selective scanning, adaptive restoration and state-of-the-art performance. Additional experiments support the existing contribution framing.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly interprets runtime measurements as evidence of near-linear scaling, greater architectural efficiency and a computational advantage over Hilbert scanning. The global/local degradation interpretation and limitation concerning unusually large, high-contrast snowflakes remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies pyiqa for perceptual evaluation, the official LC-Mamba implementation for Hilbert scanning, and the official real-snow Histoformer model source in Figure 6. It also describes retraining Mamba comparators. Existing architecture details, optimizer schedules, hardware and the promised code-release link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Morton-order precedents including PointGPT and MMamba, recent restoration and scanning references, and sources for new datasets and metrics. Section 4.3 newly attributes the correlation loss to Histoformer. These extend attribution and context while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 4 expands the training explanation into explicit Stage 1 and Stage 2 paragraphs, and related-work prose receives localized revisions. A perceptual-evaluation subsection, appendix subsections, acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist are added. The main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds eight tables covering perceptual quality, real-world evaluation, efficiency, scanning, losses and Mamba comparisons, plus an expanded feature-visualization figure. Existing qualitative panels are retained and renumbered. Table 1's ranking emphasis is corrected, Figure 6's caption changes, and the added displays substantially reorganize experimental presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for central design and applicability claims: v1's limited scan ablation and PSNR/SSIM-centered evaluation are supplemented by alternative-scan and loss controls, relevant Mamba comparators, perceptual metrics and broader quantitative real-world testing. These address important evaluation gaps. The conflicting Snow100K-Real scores in Tables 5–6 and overly broad superiority wording weaken parts of the added evidence, but the targeted experimental gains provide a substantial net improvement.
